2: Soaring up, sweeping down, bowing and bending!
25: (with a bunch of keys and a lamp, before an iron door)
35: A shudder, long unfelt, comes o’er me; Mankind’s collected woe o’erwhelms me, here. She dwells within the dark, damp walls before me, And all her crime was a delusion dear! What! I delay to free her? I dread, once again to see her? On! my shrinking but lingers Death more near.
41: (He grasps the lock: the sound of singing is heard inside.)
51: My mother, the harlot, Who put me to death; My father, the varlet, Who eaten me hath! Little sister, so good, Laid my bones in the wood, In the damp moss and clay: Then was I a beautiful bird o’ the wood; Fly away! Fly away!
59: She does not dream her lover listens near; That he the rattling chain, the rustling straw, can hear.
71: MARGARET (hiding herself on the pallet) Woe! woe! They come. O death of bitterness!
77: FAUST (whispering) Hush! hush! The hour is come that frees thee.
84: MARGARET (throwing herself before him) Art thou a man, then pity my distress!
89: FAUST Thy cries will wake the guards, and they will seize thee! (He takes hold of the fetters to unlock them.)
97: Who, headsman! unto thee such power Over me could give? Thou’rt come for me at midnight-hour: Have mercy on me, let me live! Is’t not soon enough when morning chime has run?
103:
(She rises.)

And I am yet so young, so young! And now Death comes, and ruin! I, too, was fair, and that was my undoing. My love was near, but now he’s far; Torn lies the wreath, scattered the blossoms are. Seize me not thus so violently! Spare me! What have I done to thee? Let me not vainly entreat thee! I never chanced, in all my days, to meet thee!
